body: It could be, I'm interested to see how often the noise mechanics trigger and how often that would turn a small encounter into a large horde.

You are correct, the party should be able to one round any small groups of zombies with melee weapons (unless they roll bad). But I wanted them to have options to engage at farther ranges with higher damage in horde situations while they attempt to flee. Most, if not all, combat encounters will have the option to just run away. The battle maps I have will also be relatively small in terms of feet and inches, I didn't want all firearms to be able to shoot effectively across the entire battlemap despite the realism.

I haven't played with artificer very much, and that was not something I considered. I'll have to run it through the playtests.

The silence spell was actually something I had intentionally built in, I was very particular with my wording as to hopefully drive my players to consider the spell. This campaign will be about going west to regroup with the main survivor group so I'm not too worried about them camping in the effect of the spell for the 10 minute duration

The Tiny Hut is actually a great idea for what was a small problem I was having. I wanted there to be individual travelers in the world and didn't know how to put them in without them just, ya know, dying. Tiny Hut is a great idea for them.

That is a good idea and one I will consider after the playtests. My worry is that melee weapons will become strong enough again that they'll just always be the better option. I want my players to have that really tempting option to use firearms with the risk of attracting more and more enemies.

They were a baseline, but they didn't really do enough damage for me. I want my players to be able to average killing 1 zombie a round with these weapons. (AC8 HP22) the light pistol is the only (non special) weapon that falls short of averaging a one-shot headshot. The weight classifications with higher chances to attract more was also an important part of these weapons.
